caption:
Forty stops a day and Lulu's back feels every one of them.

For couriers, tradies and reps, it's often the getting in and out that bothers the back more than the driving. Try sitting first with your feet outside, then swinging both legs in together. Reverse it to get out.

Numbness in the legs or saddle area, or bladder or bowel changes, need prompt medical attention.

Pain that hangs around for months can make every movement feel like a risk.

With persistent pain, the nervous system often turns up its protection, so things can hurt even after tissues have healed. That pain is real, and it can change.

Clinical Pilates can help by starting below your flare-up line, using reformer springs for support, and building up gradually. Flare-ups usually mean easing back for a few days, not starting over. New, changing or worsening symptoms are always worth checking with your GP or physio.

caption:
"Drink lots of water to flush out the toxins." Momo heard it after her massage, too.

It's a popular idea, but research doesn't support it. Massage doesn't release a wave of toxins, and your liver and kidneys handle waste around the clock. Feeling a bit tender or tired the next day is common and usually passes within a day or two.

A glass of water is still fine. It's just ordinary hydration, so drink to thirst.

caption:
Signed up to a gym for the new year? The first month matters most.

Lots of new starters go too hard in week one, feel wrecked, and quietly stop going. A gradual start tends to stick.

Week 1: two or three full-body sessions with light weights. Week 2: some muscle soreness is common and usually settles within a few days. Week 3: if a set feels easy, add a little weight or a couple of reps. Week 4: check your sleep, recovery and enjoyment, then keep building.

Knees or hips grumbling on hot summer walks? The pool might be your friend.

Water supports part of your body weight, so sore joints often tolerate movement more comfortably there. You don't need to swim: walking laps, side steps, knee lifts and heel raises at the edge all count, and water aerobics classes are a good option too.

Moving faster through the water adds resistance as you get stronger. Current guidelines recommend strength work on land as well, so many people do a bit of both.

Summer training in Sydney means planning around the heat. ☀️

The same pace feels harder when it's hot, because your heart rate climbs faster. Most people adapt over one to two weeks of regular, shorter sessions, so build up gradually rather than starting with your longest effort.

Train early or late, go by effort instead of pace, start well hydrated and sip regularly, and wear light, loose clothing and a hat. Stop if you feel dizzy, nauseous or get a headache that keeps building. Confusion or collapse is an emergency, so call 000.

After 50, some rotator cuff tearing is common, even in people with no pain. For many age-related tears, current guidelines suggest starting with a structured exercise program, and many people see meaningful improvement in pain and everyday function.

caption:
Ever been told your pelvis is "out"? It's one of the most common myths we hear.

Your sacroiliac joints are held by some of the strongest ligaments in the body and only move a few millimetres. Small side-to-side differences are normal, and research suggests they usually don't match who has pain.

Pain around the pelvis is more often sensitive, overloaded tissues that settle with movement and gradual loading. Adjustments can be a useful tool to ease pain and help you move, alongside exercise, not a way to put anything back.

Pain after a fall, in pregnancy, or with numbness, weakness or bladder changes is worth getting checked. Our chiropractors at Hybrid Physio are happy to explain. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Landed after a long-haul flight feeling like you've been folded in half? ✈️

Hours in a cramped seat, little movement and patchy sleep leave most people stiff. It's usually a sign you've been still for too long, not that something is wrong.

Moving first helps most: a walk in daylight and some gentle stretches on the day you land. A remedial massage a day or two later can ease the neck, back and calves, as a complement to getting moving again. Go moderate rather than deep, and plan an easy day afterwards.

Calf swelling or pain in one leg needs a doctor, not a massage. Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physio can help. Book online via the link in bio.
